what: The three corrections to clause 6.6.2, measured on a clip with 825 sparse objects and no steep ones -- fifty-five times the sparse material the first round had, and none of the confound
why: the library held ten sparse frames, one of which was also the only frame that was both sparse and steep with a large offset, and that one stayed 9,9 dB below its clip after all three corrections. Whether the residual belonged to sparse decoding or to the combination could not be told apart with ten frames, one of them confounded.

material.source: a streaming Atmos collection the user pointed at, twelve titles scanned whole: 60 369 945 object updates, 3 375 sparse objects and 83 535 coarse across eleven streams -- against 150 sparse in the whole corpus before it
material.clip: Extraction 2 (2023), frames 197 050 to 197 450 of its first Dolby track: 825 sparse objects in 55 frames and **no steep object anywhere in the clip**, so the two are separated for the first time

against_dolby.method: per frame, median over the fifteen objects. The affected set is each sparse frame and the one before it, because the written objects lag the side information

reading: with all three corrections the sparse frames sit at the level of the rest of the clip: 46,78 dB against 46,69. There is nothing left to explain in sparse decoding itself. The frame that stayed short in the earlier evidence is the one that is also steep, and its residual belongs to that combination.
